question: What is a Databricks cluster?
options: A group of Delta tables stored together
A set of computation resources (driver and worker nodes) running Spark
A collection of notebooks in a folder
A permission group for users
explanation: A cluster is a set of virtual machines, consisting of a driver node and worker nodes, that runs Apache Spark to execute your workloads.

question: What is the role of the driver node in a Spark cluster?
options: It coordinates work, maintains the SparkSession, and distributes tasks to workers
It stores all the table data permanently
It is only used for billing
It replaces the need for worker nodes
explanation: The driver hosts the SparkSession, plans jobs, and schedules/distributes tasks to the worker (executor) nodes, then collects results.

question: What does cluster autoscaling do?
options: Automatically adds or removes worker nodes based on workload demand
Automatically deletes the cluster after every job
Automatically upgrades the Spark version each night
Automatically converts all data to Parquet
explanation: Autoscaling dynamically adds workers when load is high and removes them when idle, balancing performance and cost within configured min/max bounds.

question: What is the main difference between an all-purpose cluster and a job cluster?
options: Job clusters cannot run Spark at all
All-purpose clusters cannot autoscale
All-purpose clusters are for interactive/shared use; job clusters are created for a job run and terminated after
There is no difference
explanation: All-purpose (interactive) clusters are shared for exploration and can be restarted, while job clusters are spun up to run a scheduled job and terminated when it finishes, which is more cost-effective.

question: What typically happens when a cluster is left idle beyond its auto-termination time?
options: It runs forever and keeps billing
It merges with another cluster
It deletes all your notebooks
It automatically terminates to save cost
explanation: Auto-termination shuts down an idle cluster after a configured period of inactivity, preventing unnecessary compute charges (DBUs and cloud VM cost).
